name: Ambient pad from scratch with staggered layer attacks: sine foundation with light unison, saw and triangle layers on their own filters (triangle an octave up), a separate amp envelope per layer with longer attacks for higher layers, a pitched-down foley texture in the noise slot, slow 4-bar filter LFO, panning LFO, light random on one filter and random level on the foley, then chorus, multiband compression, delay and reverb
goal: Build a lush, developing ambient pad from scratch where each layer arrives at a different time: a sine core is heard first, a saw layer fades in later and an octave-up triangle layer only blooms near the end of each held chord (so held chords get brighter and fuller over time), with a quiet tonal foley texture and slow filter/pan motion. Delta vs our pad variants: per-layer amp envelopes as the main development tool and a foley layer in the noise oscillator.

source.title: How To Make Ambient Pads 100% From Scratch (Vital Tutorial)

prerequisites: Any synth with 3 oscillators, a noise/sample slot, 2 filters, 3+ envelopes, LFOs and random modulators

inputs.name: foley_texture
inputs.description: Own recording of a clicky/ambient texture (optional)

outputs.name: pad
outputs.description: Pad whose upper layers bloom later in each held chord

constraints: Original synthesis/processing recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any DAW/synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks, impulse responses or samples copied.
Steady pitch (Matt's taste): the source also adds an LFO on oscillator pitch bend; leave it off (or tiny) here.
Use your own or free foley recordings; if tonal, pitch it to the track key.
Keep unison light on the sine core.
Drums early (Matt's taste): if the track has drums, the kick/drum loop enters by about count 8 (roughly 10-12 s), with only the pad before that.

steps.action: Osc 1: sine with a little unison as the foundation; set amp attack and release moderately long.
Osc 2: saw with unison; Osc 3: triangle with unison, pitched up one octave. Route osc 2 and osc 3 to separate filters.
Give each layer its own amp envelope (routed to its level): layer 2 a longer attack, layer 3 a much longer attack so the octave-up layer is mainly heard toward the end of each chord.
steps.expect: Held chords develop and brighten over time

steps.action: Put a quiet ambient foley texture (e.g. clicks) in the noise slot; pitch it down to the key if it is tonal.
LFO 1: triangle reshaped to open slowly and close quickly, tempo 4 bars (4/1), on one filter's cutoff. LFO 2: sine, bipolar, on osc 3 pan.
steps.expect: Slow opening sweeps and gentle stereo motion

steps.action: Add a small random modulation on the saw layer's filter and a random modulator on the foley level so it comes and goes.
FX: a bit of chorus to tie oscillators together, multiband compression to bring up subtle detail, then delay and reverb.

verification: The octave-up layer is clearly louder at the end of a held chord than at its start.
Filter sweep completes about once every 4 bars.
